newsitem.title: UK: Caspian seeks new media outlets for Leeds.
newsitem.headline: Caspian seeks new media outlets for Leeds.

text.p: Caspian Group Plc, owners of English premier league soccer club Leeds United, is aiming to take the club into a variety of new media areas, the company said on Wednesday.
Caspian said one of the options under review was the possibility of showing live matches on the Internet on a "pay-per-view" platform.

It stressed it was not seeking to disturb the lucrative television deal between BSkyB and the premier league clubs but looking at areas where intellectual property rights have not been fully defined or assigned.

Chairman Chris Akers noted that Leeds already has its own web site and has begun trial broadcast of live match commentaries via the Internet. The trials could lead to the development of "pay-per-listen" broadcasts.
Caspian, which acquired Leeds in a reverse takeover last August, reported a pro-forma loss after tax and interest of 2.63 million stg in the six months to December of last year.
Former champions Leeds have had a mediocre season, mid-table in the premier league and no success in the two domestic cup competitions.

"There is no question that, for supporters, the 1996/97 football season has been a disappointing one. However, with new management on and off the pitch, it was always going to be a period of consolidation," Akers said.
He said he was confident that investors and supporters could look forward to a promising future.

However, analysts note that heavy investment in the playing squad will be required if Leeds are to become a genuine force in English soccer once more. Caspian shares fell 1.25p to 31.25p on Wednesday.
